    "title": "C# MVVM: Add an internal test-seam constructor proactively to dependency-heavy ViewModels",
    "content": "ViewModels that wire coordinator subscriptions, event handlers, or other heavyweight dependencies in their production constructor become untestable without introducing a test seam. The proven pattern for C# MVVM is: add an `internal` constructor that accepts only the minimal data needed for unit test assertions (e.g., an observable collection), assigns all other injected services as `null!`, and is tagged with `[EditorBrowsable(EditorBrowsableState.Never)]`. Grant test-project access via `[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo(\"...Tests\")]` on the production project. This seam should be added at the time the ViewModel is first authored — retrofitting it later requires auditing `Dispose()` (see companion insight on null! + Dispose), updating tests, and triggers a rework cycle. Stub out heavy command dependencies with `() => Task.CompletedTask` lambdas.     "title": "C#: Adding a test-seam constructor with null! fields requires null-guarding Dispose() against those fields",
    "content": "When a class implements `IDisposable` and its `Dispose()` method dereferences injected dependencies, adding a test-seam constructor that assigns those dependencies as `null!` silently violates the IDisposable contract for test instances — even if production instances are never affected. The defect surfaces only when a test wraps the test-seam instance in a `using` block or calls `Dispose()` directly, causing a `NullReferenceException`. The fix is a null guard at the top of `Dispose()`: `if (_dependency is null) { /* minimal cleanup e.g. unsubscribe event handlers */ return; }`. When writing a test-seam constructor, audit every `Dispose()` method in the class for dereferences of fields the seam zeroes out and add null guards proactively — the seam and the guard must be written together.
